result.summary: Independently re-verified REQ-022 (withdraw from a registration and free the seat) at commit b401c5b, branch feature/WF02-REQ-022. Did not trust TEST-RUNNER's Step 4 report, the test report, or requirement_status.yaml history as substitutes for my own re-derivation. 1. Read docs/agents/design/REQ-022.md in full against all 5 acceptance criteria (§7's AC-to-design-element map). Every AC maps to a concrete, non-deferred design element. §0 explicitly resolves the '/my doesn't exist yet' scoping gap (standalone /withdraw command, same precedent as REQ-018/REQ-021). §6 names 4 open questions explicitly rather than silently resolving them. Confirmed 'no schema change' myself: git diff master...HEAD --stat -- apps/bot/drizzle apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts produced zero output. 2. Read apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts in full and compared it line-by-line against the design: decideWithdrawOutcome (lines 330-345) implements the exact first-match-wins table (not-found -> not-owner -> checked-in -> not-eligible -> withdrawn) in the exact stated order; withdrawRegistration (348-401) takes the FOR UPDATE row lock fresh inside its own transaction (never reusing the display-only read), writes only the admission column, and calls writeAuditLog exactly once on the one writing branch, same transaction as the UPDATE. registerForEvent's targeted change (§3) is exactly as specified: step 3 now selects `id` too, a withdrawn row's admission is normalized to null only for the decision input, and step 8 branches UPDATE-vs-INSERT with the UPDATE's SET clause naming only admission/source/qrToken (never created_at, never id) -- decideRegistrationOutcome itself is untouched (confirmed unchanged at lines 48-74). Read apps/bot/src/handlers/withdraw.ts in full: /withdraw, withdraw:confirm, withdraw:cancel all match §4 exactly, including the confirm callback's not-owner case mapping to the same generic refusedNotFound string as the not-found case (non-disclosure by construction, not just by convention). Confirmed both callback patterns registered in apps/bot/src/index.ts (lines 120-121) and the command handler registered (line 119). 3. Re-ran npm run lint myself: 0 errors, 2 pre-existing apps/web LCP warnings (Footer.tsx, Nav.tsx) -- unrelated to this diff, matches TEST-RUNNER's report. Re-ran npm run build myself: apps/web (Next.js/Turbopack) compiled successfully; apps/bot (tsc -p tsconfig.json) clean, zero errors. Re-ran npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism from the repo root myself: 17 files / 163 passed, 33 skipped (196 total) -- matches TEST-RUNNER's reported 196-test count exactly (the 33 skips are the DB-backed suite's self-skip guard when no scratch Postgres is reachable at plain `npx vitest run` time, same discipline as every prior requirement's report). 4. Stood up my own scratch Postgres (apps/bot/docker-compose.yml, port 55432) and ran `npx drizzle-kit migrate` myself -- applied cleanly with zero new migration files. Wrote my own from-scratch verification script (apps/bot/scratch-rv-req022.ts, deleted after the run) exercising the actual exported domain functions directly (not copying BACKEND-DEV's or TEST-RUNNER's scratch harnesses): - AC-security, my own fixture: seeded an owner who registered and was admitted, and a genuinely separate attacker user with NO registration of their own. Called withdrawRegistration(db, ownerRegistrationId, attackerUserId, now) directly -- returned {kind:'not-owner'}. Called withdrawRegistration with the same attacker against a well-formed but never-created UUID -- returned {kind:'not-found'}. At the domain layer these are two distinct outcome kinds (by design, so the handler layer can apply its own generic-refusal policy), and I confirmed handlers/withdraw.ts's confirm-callback switch (lines 138-142 and 149-151) maps BOTH to the identical catalog.withdraw.refusedNotFound string, closing the non-disclosure loop end-to-end from domain to user-visible text. Re-read the owner's row after both forged attempts: admission still 'admitted', updated_at and created_at byte-identical (via .getTime() comparison) to the captured 'before' values, global audit_log row count unchanged. PASS, independently reproduced. - AC4, my own fixture: register -> withdraw -> re-register cycle through the real registerForEvent/withdrawRegistration functions (capacity=5 event, single user, own event/user seeding). Captured id and created_at after the first register, again after the full cycle: same id, byte-identical created_at (.getTime() equal), exactly one row for the (event_id,user_id) pair via a direct SELECT, final admission='admitted'. PASS. - Atomic-capacity concurrency re-check on the MODIFIED registerForEvent (this is the specific confidence check this task called for, since REQ-022 touched this function's row-reuse path): capacity=1 event, 30 freshly-seeded users, all 30 calling registerForEvent concurrently via Promise.all against the real Postgres. Result: exactly 1 admitted, exactly 29 waitlisted, cross-checked by a separate direct SQL COUNT(*) against the admitted rows for that event_id (also exactly 1). No over-admission, confirming the FOR UPDATE lock discipline still holds after this requirement's targeted change to the write branch. All three checks logged PASS output; scratch script deleted, docker compose down -v torn down, git status --porcelain confirmed clean both before and after. 5. Confirmed full requirement scope: git diff master...HEAD --stat shows exactly the files the design describes (domain/registration.ts, domain/registration.db.test.ts, handlers/withdraw.ts + its test file, i18n/{types,ru,en}.ts, index.ts, plus docs/design, docs/test-specs, docs/issues/ISS-0019.yaml, and this run's own handoffs/test-report) -- nothing stray. Grepped apps/bot/src for TODO/FIXME/XXX: zero matches. git status --porcelain clean. All design-doc-listed files present: domain/registration.ts (decideWithdrawOutcome + withdrawRegistration + getRegistrationForEventAndUser + the registerForEvent row-reuse change), handlers/withdraw.ts (all 3 handlers), i18n additions (grepped: all 9 withdraw catalog keys present in types.ts/ru.ts/en.ts), index.ts wiring (command + both callback patterns registered). 6. docs/agents/requirements.yaml's REQ-022 entry (line 1148) still shows status: pending -- correct and expected at this step, DOC-UPDATER (Step 6) has not run yet. 7. Judgment on the 7 filed issues, none blocking this release: - ISS-0013 (CI has no Postgres service, MAJOR, from REQ-019): still open, still forward-looking test-infrastructure debt. Every verification in this run (mine included) executed real code against a real, locally-provisioned Postgres with real reported output, same as every prior release validation on this branch line. Not blocking. - ISS-0014 (DB-backed vitest files race under default per-file parallelism, MINOR): not applicable to any of my re-runs since I always used --no-file-parallelism for the full suite and a dedicated scratch script (no parallel file execution at all) for the DB-backed checks. Not blocking. - ISS-0015 (REQ-019 spec wording, MINOR): scoped entirely to REQ-019's own spec file, not applicable to REQ-022. - ISS-0016 (TEST-RUNNER count inflation on REQ-019, MINOR): scoped to REQ-019's own report. REQ-022's TEST-RUNNER report (196) and my own independent re-run (196: 163 passed + 33 skipped) agree exactly -- no discrepancy on this run. - ISS-0017 (REQ-020 spec fixture defects, MINOR): scoped to REQ-020's own spec file, not applicable to REQ-022. - ISS-0018 (REQ-021 spec grep list gap, MINOR): scoped to REQ-021's own spec file, not applicable to REQ-022. - ISS-0019 (REQ-022 spec has an invalid-hex UUID fixture and a grep-count collision with a pre-existing checkin catalog key, MINOR, filed this run): both are test-spec wording/fixture precision issues, not implementation defects. I did not reuse REQ-022.md's own AC-security fixture at all (I wrote an independent fixture from scratch using my own valid UUIDs and my own newly-seeded users), so my own AC-security re-verification above is not affected by and does not depend on the flagged invalid-UUID literal. The catalog key-count collision is a grep-pattern imprecision (usageNoId also exists in the unrelated pre-existing checkin catalog section) that TEST-RUNNER already correctly worked around and I did not need to re-derive, since I independently confirmed all 9 withdraw keys present in all 3 i18n files (§5 above) via my own read of the design's stated key list rather than trusting the grep count. Non-blocking; correctly left for TEST-DESIGNER to fix at the source in a future pass. Overall: every independent check I ran -- lint, build, full test suite from the repo root, an independently-constructed AC-security fixture using a genuinely separate attacker with no registration, an independently-constructed AC4 full-cycle fixture, and a fresh 30-way concurrency race against the modified registerForEvent -- agrees with all five prior gates (CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR, REVIEWER, SECURITY-REVIEWER, TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR, TEST-RUNNER). No half-implemented scope, no stray TODOs, clean git tree, all design-doc-listed files present, and the requirement's interaction with the REQ-020 atomic-capacity function it modified still holds under fresh concurrent load.
